cta.cta_text: Talk through your questions with an Edstellar assessment specialist.

items.question: What is a skills assessment?
items.answer: A skills assessment, also called a skill assessment or employee skills assessment, measures how proficient a person is in the skills their role requires, such as technical, functional, digital, leadership and soft skills. Edstellar rates each skill on one proficiency scale, so you can see the current level, the required level and the gap between them.

items.question: What is a skill proficiency assessment?
items.answer: A skill proficiency assessment rates each skill at a level, typically foundational, intermediate, advanced or expert, instead of giving a simple pass or fail. Each level has a clear description, so ratings mean the same thing across teams and locations.

items.question: How is a skills assessment different from a skills gap analysis?
items.answer: The skills assessment measures current skill proficiency. The skills gap analysis compares it with the level each role requires and ranks the gaps by importance. Edstellar delivers both, so results lead straight to learning paths and workforce plans.

items.question: Which skills can Edstellar assess?
items.answer: Edstellar assesses technical, functional and digital skills, as well as leadership and soft skills such as communication, collaboration and problem solving. Each skill area is assessed with the methods that measure it most reliably. English proficiency and cognitive ability have their own Edstellar services.

items.question: Which methods are used in a skills assessment?
items.answer: Depending on the skill, Edstellar combines knowledge tests, practical simulations, work samples and project reviews, competency-based interviews, manager ratings, self-assessment and certification records. Using more than one method gives a verified level instead of a single self-rating.

items.question: How are proficiency levels defined?
items.answer: Edstellar sets the proficiency levels with your subject matter experts during job analysis, writing a clear description of what each level looks like in the role. Your existing competency framework or skills framework can be the starting point, so the competency assessment reflects how your organization already describes each role.

items.question: How do skills assessments support upskilling and reskilling?
items.answer: The skills gap analysis shows which gaps matter most for each role and team. Edstellar turns those gaps into targeted learning paths, connected to training, coaching and on-the-job practice, and reassesses afterwards to confirm progress. The same data feeds skills-based workforce planning.

items.question: Can skills assessments support internal mobility?
items.answer: Yes. Verified skill proficiency shows who is ready for new roles, projects or career paths, so internal moves, talent mobility and career development rest on evidence rather than job titles alone.

items.question: How long does a skills assessment take?
items.answer: Time per employee depends on the number of skills and methods, and is agreed at scoping. A typical engagement takes about six weeks from kickoff to learning paths, and skills assessments run online across locations.

items.question: How is skills assessment data protected?
items.answer: Skills data is collected only for the agreed purpose, access is limited to agreed stakeholders, and reports are shared under the confidentiality terms set at scoping. Edstellar holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for information security management.

items.question: How much does a skills assessment cost?
items.answer: Cost depends on the number of roles, people and skills, the methods used, and how much gap analysis and learning path design you need. Edstellar scopes each skills assessment before quoting, so you pay only for what your decision requires.
